newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo creates new Eduscho board after purchase.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo creates new Eduscho board after purchase.

text.p: Tchibo Holding AG in a statement on Monday said it had formed a five-strong management board at coffee roasting firm Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, which it bought last December, with immediate effect.
German cartel authorities last week approved Tchibo's acquisition of Eduscho, retroactive to January 1, 1997.

Tchibo said it would retain former Eduscho top managers Hans-Werner Eckhoff (procurement and production) and Bernd Schmielau (personnel and legal matters) and it had newly appointed Reinhold Moebs, formerly of Procter & Gamble, as marketing head.
Tchibo also added two of its own managers to the Eduscho board -- Hasso von Duering as sales director and Rainer Kutzner to head finance/systems.
Former Eduscho sales head Hartmut Felgen had left the company, the statement said.

The purchase enables Tchibo to control a similar share -- around 30 percent -- of Germany's roasted coffee market as currently held by market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard, which is part of Philip Morris.
So far it plans to run the two companies separately.
